chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to me, saying: 'Abaad ibn Sulayman narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Daylami from his father, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Has the news of the Overwhelming Calamity (Al-Ghashiyah) come to you? He replied: The Qaim (peace be upon him) will overwhelm them with the sword.
I said: 'Faces, that Day, humbled.' He replied: It means submissive, and they will not be able to resist.
I said: 'Laboring.' He replied: They worked with that which Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, did not send down.
I said: 'Toiling.' He replied: They set themselves against those who are not the leaders of the affair.
I said: 'Entering into burning fire.' He replied: They will enter the fire of war in the world during the era of the Qaim (peace be upon him), and in the Hereafter, Hell.

key_terms.الْغاشِیَهِ: The Overwhelming Calamity, referring to Surah Al-Ghashiyah
key_terms.الْقَائِمُ: The Qaim (The Riser), a title for Imam al-Mahdi (a.s.)
key_terms.جَهَنَّمَ: Hell, the abode of punishment in the Hereafter
key_terms.نَارُ الْحَرْبِ: The Fire of War, referring to worldly conflicts
key_terms.وُلَاهُ الْأَمْرِ: The Leaders of the Affair, referring to the Imams

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the verses in Surah Al-Ghashiyah according to Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.)?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq presents this hadith as a specific exegetical tradition (tafsir) linking the eschatological descriptions in Surah Al-Ghashiyah to the era of Imam al-Mahdi (a.s.), emphasizing the political and spiritual reality of his rule. The narration clarifies that the 'humbled faces' and 'burning fire' are not merely abstract concepts but manifest as the subjugation of enemies by the sword and the dual punishment of worldly wars and hereafter Hellfire during the Qaim's reign.
